title: The Virtual Biotech: a multi-agent AI framework for drug development decisions
summary: The Virtual Biotech journal abstract reports a human-guided multi-agent analysis of 55,984 trials. Drugs targeting cell-type-specific genes were associated with a 48% greater likelihood of reaching market and 32% fewer adverse events. The system also proposed a lung-cancer strategy and inferred possible reasons for a terminated ulcerative-colitis trial. These are retrospective associations and hypotheses, not demonstrated treatment benefits. The date represents the 2026-10-22 journal version; the linked preprint, including the same reported association, first appeared on 2026-02-23.
ai_technology: Virtual Biotech multi-agent AI framework (more than 37,000 agents)

evidence.tested: Retrospective trial-outcome/target-feature analysis across 55,984 trials, plus computational therapeutic and trial-failure hypotheses.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: More than 37,000 AI agents annotated trial outcomes and integrated multimodal evidence to propose and analyze therapeutic decisions.
